claims.text: Mainly bacteriostatic; bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibit protein synthesis.
claims.quote: Macrolides are antibiotics that are primarily bacteriostatic; by binding to the 50S subunit of the ribosome, they inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.

claims.text: CAP (MSD): outpatient, no comorbidities: amoxicillin + a macrolide (azithromycin or clarithromycin) or doxycycline;
claims.quote: Amoxicillin plus either Macrolide (azithromycin or clarithromycin) or Doxycycline (if allergic to macrolides)
claims.locator: Table: Antibiotic Therapy for Bacterial Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults › I

claims.text: outpatient with comorbidities: a beta-lactam + macrolide or doxycycline;
claims.quote: Beta-lactam (cefpodoxime, cefuroxime, amoxicillin, or amoxicillin/clavulanic acid) plus either Macrolide or doxycycline
claims.locator: Table: Antibiotic Therapy for Bacterial Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults › II

claims.text: inpatient non-ICU: azithromycin + a beta-lactam (or an antipneumococcal FQ alone);
claims.quote: Azithromycin plus Beta-lactam (eg, cefotaxime, ceftriaxone, ceftaroline) or Antipneumococcal fluoroquinolone orally or intravenously (alone)
claims.locator: Table: Antibiotic Therapy for Bacterial Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults › III

claims.text: ICU: beta-lactam + an antipneumococcal FQ or azithromycin.
claims.quote: Beta-lactam (cefotaxime or ceftriaxone) plus either Antipneumococcal fluoroquinolone or Azithromycin
claims.locator: Table: Antibiotic Therapy for Bacterial Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults › IVA

claims.text: Azithromycin (adult): CAP 500 mg day 1, then 250 mg daily days 2–5;
claims.quote: Community-acquired pneumonia Pharyngitis/tonsillitis (second-line therapy) Skin/skin structure (uncomplicated) | 500 mg as a single dose on Day 1, followed by 250 mg once daily on Days 2 through 5

claims.text: AECOPD 500 mg daily × 3 days or the same 5-day course.
claims.quote: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease | 500 mg once daily for 3 days OR 500 mg as a single dose on Day 1, followed by 250 mg once daily on Days 2 through 5

claims.text: No renal dose adjustment.
claims.quote: For azithromycin, no dosage adjustment is required for renal insufficiency.

claims.text: GI upset (mainly erythromycin; less with clarithromycin/azithromycin; food helps).
claims.quote: Erythromycin commonly causes dose-related GI disturbances, including nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea; disturbances are less common with clarithromycin and azithromycin. Taking the medication with food may help decrease GI disturbances.

claims.text: QT prolongation/torsades (erythromycin most;
claims.quote: Erythromycin causes QT-interval prolongation and predisposes to ventricular tachyarrhythmia

claims.text: clarithromycin/azithromycin less likely to cause arrhythmia).
claims.quote: Clarithromycin and azithromycin may also cause QT-interval prolongation but are less likely to cause arrhythmias.

claims.text: Severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity (azithromycin label).
claims.quote: Hepatotoxicity: Severe, and sometimes fatal, hepatotoxicity has been reported.

claims.text: Erythromycin: tinnitus/reversible hearing loss, cholestatic jaundice;
claims.quote: Erythromycin may cause dose-related tinnitus, dizziness, and reversible hearing loss. Cholestatic jaundice occurs most commonly with erythromycin

claims.text: avoid in neonates (pyloric stenosis).
claims.quote: Erythromycin should be avoided in neonates unless no other options are available because of the risk for infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

claims.text: May worsen myasthenia gravis.
claims.quote: ZITHROMAX may exacerbate muscle weakness in persons with myasthenia gravis.

claims.text: Prior cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with that macrolide.
claims.quote: ZITHROMAX is contraindicated in patients with a history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with prior use of azithromycin.

claims.text: Clarithromycin: with lovastatin/simvastatin/lomitapide, with colchicine in renal or hepatic impairment,
claims.quote: • Colchicine in renal or hepatic impairment ( 4.4 ) • Lomitapide, lovastatin, and simvastatin ( 4.5 )

claims.text: with cisapride/pimozide (fatal arrhythmias).
claims.quote: Concomitant administration of macrolides with astemizole, cisapride, pimozide, or terfenadine is contraindicated because potentially fatal cardiac arrhythmias

claims.text: Caution with known QT prolongation or other QT drugs.
claims.quote: This risk which can be fatal should be considered in patients with certain cardiovascular disorders including known QT prolongation or history torsades de pointes, those with proarrhythmic conditions, and with other drugs that prolong th

claims.text: Erythromycin and clarithromycin inhibit CYP450 (azithromycin least):
claims.quote: Erythromycin and, to some extent, clarithromycin interact with numerous medications because they inhibit hepatic metabolism via the cytochrome P-450 (CYP450) system. Azithromycin is the least likely to interact with other medications.

claims.text: ↑ INR with warfarin, rhabdomyolysis with lovastatin/simvastatin, somnolence with midazolam/triazolam, theophylline toxicity, ↑ tacrolimus/cyclosporine/ergots.
claims.quote: Warfarin: Further elevation of the prothrombin time/international normalized ratio (PT/INR) - Lovastatin and simvastatin: Rhabdomyolysis - Midazolam and triazolam: Somnolence - Theophylline: Nausea, vomiting, and seizures - Tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and ergot alkaloids: Elevated serum levels of these medications

claims.text: Take with food if GI upset.
claims.quote: Taking the medication with food may help decrease GI disturbances.

claims.text: Stop and seek care for signs of hepatitis.
claims.quote: Discontinue ZITHROMAX immediately if signs and symptoms of hepatitis occur.
